```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(islandbrand)
options(islh.embed_fonts = FALSE)
widgets_available <- requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("reactable", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = widgets_available)
```

Use `islh_plotly()` to add hover labels and zoom to an existing ggplot, and
`islh_reactable()` to give a data frame search, sorting and pagination. Both
return ordinary HTML widgets. They run in the reader's browser without a
server, an online account or an internet connection when resources are
embedded in the report.

## Set up once

Install the optional packages, then restart R:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
islandbrand::islh_install_deps("html", interactive = TRUE)
```

At the top of your report:

```{r report-setup, eval=FALSE}
library(islandbrand)
islh_setup(format = "html")
```

The interactive packages are optional. Existing static reports keep their
current dependencies. To check readiness without installing anything, use
`islh_check("html", interactive = TRUE)`.

## Make a plot interactive

Start with prepared counts, such as those returned by
`islandepi::islh_count_events()`. This example uses simulated weekly counts:

```{r counts}
weekly <- data.frame(
  week = seq(as.Date("2026-01-04"), by = "week", length.out = 12),
  cases = c(10, 12, 18, 29, 40, 52, 45, 31, 24, 18, 14, 10)
)

p <- islh_epi_curve(
  weekly, date = week, count = cases,
  title = "Reported cases by week",
  subtitle = "Simulated surveillance counts",
  caption = "Source: simulated example data"
)
```

```{r interactive-curve}
islh_plotly(p, height = 380)
```

Hover over a bar to see its values. Drag to zoom into a date range and
double-click to reset. With grouped plots, click the legend to hide or show a
series. Page scrolling stays enabled when the pointer is over the plot.

Hover labels show the original reporting date and the count for that period
and group. The bar's centre is offset for drawing; it is not the reporting
date. The same labels apply to case tiles. Reference bands and lines identify
their limits or mean, and year separators have no tooltip. With custom plot
labels, such as `ggplot2::labs(x = "Week starting", y = "Reported cases")`,
the tooltip uses those labels too.

Ordinary ggplots work too. The helper applies the Island Health theme, keeps
the plot's layers and scales, and puts its title, subtitle and caption outside
the panel so zooming cannot hide them:

```{r scatter}
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  datasets::mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(colour = islh_brand("primary")) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Fuel economy by vehicle weight",
    x = "Weight (1,000 lb)", y = "Miles per US gallon"
  )

islh_plotly(p, tooltip = c("x", "y"), height = 340)
```

You can continue with `plotly::layout()` or `plotly::config()`. Plotly's
conversion does not support every extension geom, map coordinate system or
theme feature. Check the result before sharing; retain a static ggplot for
figures that do not convert well. Interactive plots also need a text summary
or accompanying table for readers who cannot use hover or drag controls.

## Make a table interactive

```{r interactive-table}
islh_reactable(
  weekly, title = "Weekly counts",
  source_note = "Source: simulated example data",
  page_size = 5, filterable = TRUE
)
```

Type in the search box, click a column heading to sort, or move between pages.
Column filters are optional; search, sorting and pagination are enabled by
default. Missing values display as `n/a`.

Pass standard reactable arguments for more control. Numeric values remain
numeric, so formatting does not change their sort order:

```{r formatted-table}
islh_reactable(
  weekly,
  title = "Most recent weeks first",
  columns = list(
    week = reactable::colDef(name = "Week starting"),
    cases = reactable::colDef(
      name = "Reported cases",
      format = reactable::colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE)
    )
  ),
  defaultSorted = list(week = "desc"),
  page_size = 5
)
```

Use `groupBy = "area"` to group rows when the data has an `area` column.
Titles and source notes are plain text. Cell values are escaped by default;
enable `html = TRUE` in a column definition only for trusted markup.

## Share a complete report

In Quarto, set `embed-resources: true` so scripts, styles and fonts travel in
one HTML file. The package's `islh-report-html` format already sets this.
For R Markdown use `html_document` with `self_contained: true`.

Put each widget in its own chunk, as the last expression; do not wrap it in
`print()` or use `results: asis`. To use the complete Quarto example:

```{r example-path, eval=FALSE}
file.copy(
  system.file("examples", "interactive.qmd", package = "islandbrand"),
  "interactive.qmd"
)
```

Open that file and render it to HTML. Fonts follow the `islh_setup()` setting:
installed BC Sans faces are embedded by default, with a warning and fallback
when unavailable. Use `embed_fonts = FALSE` to omit font embedding when every
reader already has the font or file size matters. This guide omits embedded
fonts to keep the package documentation small.

For a single standalone widget:

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(
  islh_reactable(weekly, title = "Weekly counts"),
  "weekly-counts.html", selfcontained = TRUE
)
```

## Reports that also render to Word

Interactive widgets require HTML. Choose a static output for the other
format; the helpers give a clear error if used during a non-HTML render:

```{r multiple-formats, eval=FALSE}
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  islh_plotly(p)
} else {
  p
}
```

```{r multiple-table-formats, eval=FALSE}
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  islh_reactable(weekly)
} else {
  islh_flextable(weekly)
}
```

## Prepare values before sharing

The HTML contains the data supplied to each widget, including hidden columns,
rows on other pages and values omitted from hover labels. Hiding a field does
not remove it from the file. Select the intended columns and apply approved
suppression rules before creating a widget. For example, use
`islandepi::islh_suppress_table()` for counts and linked rates, then select
only the resulting display columns. These helpers do not infer suppression
thresholds or authorise data for release.
